prompt: I'm testing about 1,000 sorghum test-cross hybrids per site at several locations in two-row plots. Seed lets me replicate maybe 30% of them, and I have 10 commercial checks. How should I lay it out and analyse it?

source.citation: Velazco et al. 2017, Theor Appl Genet 130:1375-1392
source.basis: 21 trials, p-rep (~30% replicated twice), 10 checks, 34-86 rows x 20-40 cols, SpATS

reference_plan.design: Resolvable p-rep: ~30% of hybrids in two plots (one in each half of the field, giving two resolvable blocks), ~70% once; checks replicated more often and spread across the grid.
reference_plan.layout: Rectangular grid (e.g. ~45 rows x 30 columns for ~1,350 plots) with a ring of border plots; coordinates recorded for every plot.
reference_plan.replication: Replication comes from repeated hybrids, checks and locations; plan for 3-29% plot loss.
reference_plan.randomization: Randomize within each half; record the seed.
reference_plan.analysis: Per site: SpATS (genotype + 2-D P-spline + random row and column); then combine BLUEs across sites.
pitfalls: Losing unreplicated entries to missing plots
Running non-spatial analysis on a large trial

notes: Spatial models cut residual variance by 49% (yield) in the source trials.

prompt: 70 sorghum varieties under low-phosphorus conditions on a farmer-like field where the soil is very patchy. I can do two or three reps.

source.citation: Leiser et al. 2012, J Agron Crop Sci
source.basis: 17 trials, 70 genotypes, Mali; plant-available P CV 39%; AR1xAR1 gained ~10 points of heritability over RCB

reference_plan.design: Alpha-lattice with incomplete blocks of 7 plots (70 = 10 x 7) per rep; prefer 3 reps on patchy soil.
reference_plan.layout: Compact blocks, long axis across the visible gradient; reps side by side; border ring.
reference_plan.replication: 3 reps per site; 2 reps only if the analysis will be spatial.
reference_plan.randomization: agricolae alpha generator with recorded seed.
reference_plan.analysis: Compare lattice model with AR1xAR1 (+ random row/col); keep the best by AIC/residual plots.
pitfalls: Blocks laid along the gradient
Treating two reps as enough without spatial analysis

notes: Gains from spatial models were largest under low P and with two reps.

prompt: First-stage sugarcane selection: about 440 families at two sites, one of them sandy and low fertility. Incomplete blocks with two checks per block. I could map the soil if it's worth it.

source.citation: Cursi et al. 2021, Front Plant Sci 12:749533
source.basis: EM38 ECa >10,000 readings/site; AR1xAR1 raised H2 from 0.35 to 0.72 on sandy site

reference_plan.design: Incomplete blocks with 2 checks in every block (as planned), 2 reps if seedlings allow.
reference_plan.layout: Georeferenced grid; ECa survey (two depths) about 30 days after planting; soil grid ~7-9 points/ha.
reference_plan.replication: 2 reps per site; checks in every block give tray-like block correction.
reference_plan.randomization: Random within blocks; record seed.
reference_plan.analysis: Baseline vs +covariate vs AR1xAR1 vs AR1xAR1 + covariate; forward-select covariates.
pitfalls: Expecting covariates alone to fix spatial trend (spatial error structure gave most of the gain)

notes: Mapping matters most on sandy, low-fertility soil.

prompt: I want to test 3 wheat cultivars across a range of water levels using one sprinkler line down the middle of the field, with 3 blocks.

source.citation: Hanks et al. 1980, Soil Sci Soc Am J 44:886-888 (agridat::hanks.sprinkler)
source.basis: Line-source, 6 levels per side, 3 genotypes x 3 blocks; Toeplitz correlation along distance

reference_plan.design: Line-source: cultivars as strips perpendicular to the line within each block; subplots at fixed distances on both sides (e.g. 6 per side).
reference_plan.layout: Catch cans at each distance to measure actual water applied; buffer beyond the last subplot.
reference_plan.replication: 3 blocks; cultivar randomized within block; irrigation is NOT randomized.
reference_plan.randomization: Randomize cultivar strip order within each block.
reference_plan.analysis: cultivar x irrigation x side fixed; block, block:side, block:irrigation random; Toeplitz or distance-based correlation within block:cultivar.
pitfalls: Treating distance levels as randomized treatments
Wind skewing the gradient to one side

notes: Water level is set by distance from the line, so inference about irrigation relies on the model.

prompt: 30 oilseed rape varieties, a mix of tall hybrids and short open-pollinated types, in 1.5 m plots side by side, 4 reps.

source.citation: Büchse, GCIRC Bulletin 18
source.basis: Interplot interference up to ~5%; double-width plots or core harvest; group by height/type

reference_plan.design: Group varieties by type/height (e.g. 4 groups) as whole plots, varieties randomized within groups; or keep RCBD but use double-width plots.
reference_plan.layout: 3.0 m plots harvested whole, or 3.0 m plots with only the central 1.5 m harvested; border ring.
reference_plan.replication: 4 reps.
reference_plan.randomization: Groups randomized within rep; varieties within group.
reference_plan.analysis: Split-plot model if grouped; between-group comparisons have whole-plot error.
pitfalls: Short varieties ranked low because they sit next to tall hybrids

notes: Double-width plots were expected to halve interference.

prompt: Progeny rows: about 3,000 soybean lines, one plot each at one site because seed is limited. I can repeat a handful of checks many times.

source.citation: Carroll et al. 2024, Crop Sci 64:3135-3152
source.basis: ~10 checks x ~46 reps per field; P-splines 168% and soil-ML 181% relative efficiency

reference_plan.design: Checks spread systematically (diagonal or regular grid) through the field, ~5-10% of plots; entries randomized to the remaining plots.
reference_plan.layout: Row x column grid with coordinates; optional soil sampling or ECa map.
reference_plan.replication: Entries unreplicated; checks give error and trend.
reference_plan.randomization: Random allocation of entries (required for moving-grid adjustment).
reference_plan.analysis: P-spline (SpATS/statgenSTA) spatial model; check-based relative efficiency to compare adjustments.
pitfalls: Planting families in contiguous blocks (invalidates moving grid)
Too few checks to see the trend

notes: Spatial adjustment only helps when yield is spatially autocorrelated.

prompt: Managed-drought trial for 60 maize hybrids. Drip tape laterals run every 4 rows, fed from a main along the north edge; in drought plots I turn the drip off after flowering. 3 reps.

source.citation: Design logic: split-plot as in Bhattarai et al. 2020 (doi:10.1002/csc2.20171); water gradient handling as in Hanks et al. 1980
source.basis: Water regime applied per lateral group belongs on whole plots

reference_plan.design: Split-plot: water regime on whole plots (groups of laterals), 60 hybrids randomized within each whole plot (alpha sub-blocks of 6 or 10 if whole plots are long).
reference_plan.layout: Blocks run east-west at a constant distance from the north main; buffer rows (or a dry alley) between irrigated and drought whole plots to stop lateral water movement.
reference_plan.replication: 3 reps gives only 2 df for the water test; consider 4-6 reps if the water main effect matters.
reference_plan.randomization: Water regime randomized to whole plots within each block; hybrids within whole plots.
reference_plan.analysis: y ~ water*hybrid + (1|block) + (1|block:water) + spatial terms within whole plots.
pitfalls: Pressure drop along laterals far from the main
Seepage into drought plots from neighbouring irrigated plots
Turning drip off on a different date per rep

notes: Ask where the main and laterals are before drawing any layout.

prompt: 120 wheat lines, 3 reps, sown and harvested with a plot combine in serpentine order. There might be a gradient but I don't know which way it runs.

source.citation: Gilmour, Cullis & Verbyla 1997, JABES 2:269-293; Rodríguez-Álvarez et al. 2018 (SpATS)
source.basis: Extraneous row/column variation from field operations; AR1xAR1 dominates

reference_plan.design: Resolvable row-column (each rep a rectangle, e.g. 10 x 12) or alpha-lattice with k = 10 or 12 plus row/column terms.
reference_plan.layout: Reps side by side; record row, column and the serpentine harvest order.
reference_plan.replication: 3 reps.
reference_plan.randomization: Within rep; seed recorded.
reference_plan.analysis: genotype + rep + random row and column + AR1xAR1 or SpATS; inspect variogram.
pitfalls: Harvest drift (moisture, combine calibration) aligned with serpentine order

notes: When gradient direction is unknown, row-column designs cover both directions.

prompt: Single-plant selection nursery: 2,000 spaced plants from 40 families, no replication. Can I adjust for soil differences?

source.citation: Technow, mvngGrAd R package vignette
source.basis: Moving-grid adjustment requires random allocation and no self-influence

reference_plan.design: Randomize individual plants (not family blocks) over the grid; add repeated check plants if possible.
reference_plan.layout: Regular grid with coordinates for every plant.
reference_plan.replication: None for individuals; checks or the moving grid supply the environmental estimate.
reference_plan.randomization: Complete randomization of plants to grid positions.
reference_plan.analysis: Moving-grid adjustment excluding the centre cell; or 2-D P-splines.
pitfalls: Family-block planting biases moving-grid adjustment
Strong competition makes neighbour correlation negative

notes: Check covariate-response correlation before adjusting.

prompt: Wheat in an automated imaging greenhouse with conveyor lanes, 33 lines x 2 salt levels x 8 reps (528 carts). Plants germinate in a normal greenhouse first, then move to the conveyor.

source.citation: Brien et al. 2013, Plant Methods 9:5
source.basis: Two-phase experiment; small E-W and large N-S trends; rotation increased error

reference_plan.design: Blocks = groups of lanes/positions small enough to be homogeneous (row-column on lanes x positions); salt x line randomized within blocks.
reference_plan.layout: Germination-phase blocks map onto conveyor blocks ('big with big').
reference_plan.replication: 8 reps as blocks.
reference_plan.randomization: Two-stage randomization recorded for both phases.
reference_plan.analysis: line*salt + block + lane/position terms + linear N-S trend.
pitfalls: Relying on cart rotation instead of design
Phase-1 positions ignored

notes: Rotation only works if plants spend equal time in every microclimate.

prompt: Greenhouse bay: door at the south end, cooling pad on the east wall, fans on the west, overhead sprinklers. 8 benches. Testing 24 tomato genotypes x 2 nitrogen levels, 4 plants per combination.

source.citation: Design logic from Brien et al. 2013 (doi:10.1186/1746-4811-9-5), Poorter et al. 2012 (doi:10.1071/FP12028), Hartung et al. 2019
source.basis: Local microclimate sources create gradients; block across them

reference_plan.design: Pad-fan cooling makes an east-west temperature gradient: run benches north-south so each bench sits at one temperature and use benches (or bench pairs) as blocks; 48 genotype x N combinations per block.
reference_plan.layout: Guard plants on bench ends nearest the door and pad; no measured plants under sprinkler overlap edges or next to the door.
reference_plan.replication: 4 blocks (pairs of benches), one plant per combination per block.
reference_plan.randomization: Randomize combinations within each block; if N is delivered by fertigation zone, put N on whole plots (split-plot).
reference_plan.analysis: genotype*N + block (+ position trend); split-plot error for N if zoned.
pitfalls: Overhead sprinklers giving uneven water or leaching N
Door draughts on the south end
Nitrogen applied by hand in group order

notes: Sketch the bay with every source marked before randomizing.

prompt: Drought study on 12 sorghum lines in 2 L pots. Plants will reach about 40 g dry mass by the end. I water by hand with a measuring cup.

source.citation: Poorter et al. 2012, Funct Plant Biol 39:821-838
source.basis: Pots too small above ~2 g dry mass per L; water gravimetrically

reference_plan.design: Factorial line x water in RCBD with benches as blocks.
reference_plan.layout: Pots of at least ~20 L for 40 g plants (2 g/L rule), white or foil-wrapped; fixed substrate mass per pot.
reference_plan.replication: Set by power on ln(biomass); expect SD of ln(dry mass) 0.2-0.6.
reference_plan.randomization: Within bench; watering order by block.
reference_plan.analysis: line*water + block; drought defined by target soil water content, not volume added.
pitfalls: 40 g in 2 L = 20 g/L: roots pot-bound, drought starts in controls too
Volume watering makes drought depend on plant size

notes: Use gravimetric watering to a target weight.

prompt: Heat stress on Arabidopsis: 22 C vs 30 C. I have 4 identical chambers and can do 2 runs, 30 plants per chamber.

source.basis: Identical chambers and runs differ; chamber is the unit

reference_plan.design: Run 1: 2 chambers at 22 C, 2 at 30 C (random). Run 2: swap assignments. True n = 4 chamber-runs per temperature.
reference_plan.layout: Within each chamber, block by shelf; corners filled with guard plants.
reference_plan.replication: 4 chamber-runs per level; 30 plants per chamber are subsamples (average or (1|run:chamber)).
reference_plan.randomization: Temperature to chamber per run; plant positions within chamber.
reference_plan.analysis: y ~ temperature + (1|run) + (1|run:chamber) (+ (1|run:chamber:shelf)).
pitfalls: One chamber per temperature (confounded)
Skipping a uniformity pilot

notes: Run a short uniformity pilot (fresh weight, flower count) first.

prompt: Elevated CO2 (800 ppm) vs ambient on wheat in walk-in chambers. The CO2 is injected from gas cylinders and controlled by the chamber analyser.

source.citation: Porter et al. 2015, Plant Methods
source.basis: CO2 analyser fault traced via d13C; independent sensors recommended

reference_plan.design: >=2 chambers per CO2 level or repeated runs swapping levels.
reference_plan.layout: Independent CO2 logger in each chamber at canopy height; limit door openings.
reference_plan.replication: Chamber-runs are the units.
reference_plan.randomization: CO2 level to chamber per run.
reference_plan.analysis: y ~ co2 + (1|run) + (1|run:chamber).
pitfalls: Analyser zero drift injecting excess CO2
People in the chamber raising CO2

notes: Cylinder CO2 is 13C-depleted, so leaf d13C reveals how much was injected.

prompt: I have 200 Arabidopsis accessions for flowering time and only 48-cell trays (6 x 8) on 3 shelves in one chamber. I can't replicate everything. Can I put Col-0 in every tray instead?

source.citation: Augmented design (Federer 1956); p-rep (Cullis et al. 2006, doi:10.1198/108571106X154443); corner/edge effects (Potvin et al. 1990; Poorter et al. 2012)
source.basis: Repeated checks estimate block (tray) effects so entries need no replication

reference_plan.design: Augmented-by-tray: Col-0 and a second check (e.g. Ler, different flowering time) once in every tray; accessions spread across trays. With guard edges a 6 x 8 tray has 24 interior cells: 2 checks + 22 accessions, so 10 trays.
reference_plan.layout: Edge cells hold guard plants; trays distributed over the 3 shelves; avoid chamber corners.
reference_plan.replication: Accessions unreplicated; consider replicating ~20% (p-rep) if 2-3 extra trays fit.
reference_plan.randomization: make_tray_design(): random accession-to-tray and cell positions; record seed.
reference_plan.analysis: y ~ genotype + (1|tray) using checks to estimate tray effects (or shelf + cell position terms).
pitfalls: Bottom-watering whole trays makes tray the unit for any water treatment
One check that flowers outside the accessions' range adjusts poorly

notes: Two checks with contrasting phenotypes estimate tray effects more robustly than one.

prompt: We compared leaf growth of 3 Arabidopsis accessions and got a different ranking than another lab. How do I make the result robust?

source.citation: Massonnet et al. 2010, Plant Physiol 152:2142-2157
source.basis: 10 labs, standardized protocol; light quality and handling explained differences

reference_plan.design: Repeat the experiment over >=3 independent runs (blocks), ideally in 2 chambers or facilities.
reference_plan.layout: Blocks within chamber; same pot, substrate and handling SOP.
reference_plan.replication: Plants within run are subsamples of run x accession for reproducibility claims.
reference_plan.randomization: Positions within chamber each run.
reference_plan.analysis: accession + (1|run) + (1|run:accession); report run x accession variance.
pitfalls: Different light quality between facilities
Handling (watering, sampling time) differing between runs

notes: Molecular profiles carried strong lab effects even when growth matched.

prompt: Four nutrient solutions on maize seedlings, all in one growth chamber, 48 pots on 4 shelves.

source.citation: Potvin et al. 1990, Can J Bot 68:499-504
source.basis: Corners poor, centre best; block within chambers; each treatment at least twice per block

reference_plan.design: RCBD with shelves as blocks: 12 pots per shelf = 4 nutrients x 3 pots.
reference_plan.layout: Corner positions hold guard pots; lamp height adjusted per shelf; PAR mapped.
reference_plan.replication: 12 pots per nutrient (3 per shelf); pots must be individually supplied (not one shared reservoir per nutrient).
reference_plan.randomization: Within shelf.
reference_plan.analysis: nutrient + (1|shelf); add position terms if PAR map shows gradients.
pitfalls: One hydroponic tank per nutrient makes the tank the unit (n = 1)

notes: Ask how solutions are delivered before calling pots replicates.

prompt: Pilot of a new compound in mice: vehicle plus 3 doses, so 4 groups. There's no prior SD for the endpoint.

source.citation: Arifin & Zahiruddin 2017, Malays J Med Sci 24:101-105; Festing & Altman 2002
source.basis: Resource equation: error df 10-20

reference_plan.design: Randomized block design (blocks = batch or cage racks), 4 dose groups.
reference_plan.layout: Mixed cages if dosing is individual.
reference_plan.replication: Resource equation for k = 4: 4 to 6 mice per group (more if attrition expected); replace with a power analysis once an SD exists.
reference_plan.randomization: Within blocks; blinded outcome assessment.
reference_plan.analysis: dose + block; trend test across doses.
pitfalls: Treating the resource equation as a power analysis
Copying n from unrelated studies

notes: Planning recommendation only; IACUC review required.

prompt: Does the drug effect depend on strain and sex? Two strains, both sexes, drug vs vehicle.

source.citation: Shaw et al. 2002, ILAR J 43:223-232; Garcia-Sifuentes & Maney 2021
source.basis: Factorials reduce animal use and test interactions

reference_plan.design: 2 x 2 x 2 factorial in randomized blocks (batches).
reference_plan.layout: Single-sex, single-strain cages; drug mixed within cages if individually dosed.
reference_plan.replication: Power for the drug x strain or drug x sex interaction if that is the question (needs ~4x the n of a main effect).
reference_plan.randomization: Within strain x sex x batch.
reference_plan.analysis: drug*strain*sex + batch (+ (1|cage)).
pitfalls: Separate experiments per strain/sex, then comparing p-values

notes: Planning recommendation only.

prompt: Microbiome study: antibiotics vs control in the drinking water, 10 mice per group housed 5 per cage.

source.citation: McCafferty et al. 2013, ISME J 7:2116-2125; ARRIVE 2.0 item 1b
source.basis: Cage effects develop over weeks; drinking-water treatment makes cage the unit

reference_plan.design: Cage-level randomization with more, smaller cages: e.g. 5 cages x 2 mice per group instead of 2 x 5.
reference_plan.layout: Cages interleaved on the rack; baseline faecal samples before treatment.
reference_plan.replication: n = cages per group (currently 2, which gives almost no df).
reference_plan.randomization: Antibiotic to cage; cages balanced by litter/source.
reference_plan.analysis: Mixed model or PERMANOVA with cage as the unit (strata = cage).
pitfalls: Two cages per group: treatment confounded with cage

notes: Planning recommendation only.

prompt: Behaviour study in male BALB/c mice with 3 treatment groups. Should I single-house them?

source.citation: Kappel, Hawkins & Mendl 2017, Animals 7:88
source.basis: Housing choice is context dependent; aggression vs isolation

reference_plan.design: RCBD with cage or batch as block; same housing for every group.
reference_plan.layout: If group-housed, mix treatments within cages (individual dosing) and record social rank/wounds; if single-housed, justify and provide enrichment.
reference_plan.replication: Set by power; account for removals due to fighting.
reference_plan.randomization: Within cage/batch; test order randomized.
reference_plan.analysis: treatment + block (+ (1|cage)).
pitfalls: Single-housing only some groups
Fighting-related removals concentrated in one group

notes: Planning recommendation only.

prompt: Von Frey pain thresholds after nerve injury vs sham. Two technicians, one man and one woman, will test the mice.

source.citation: Sorge et al. 2014, Nat Methods 11:629-632
source.basis: Male experimenters induce stress analgesia

reference_plan.design: Experimenter as a blocking factor: each technician tests equal numbers of injured and sham mice (or one technician tests all).
reference_plan.layout: Same room, time of day and habituation for both.
reference_plan.replication: Set by power on threshold SD.
reference_plan.randomization: Testing order randomized; tester blinded to surgery.
reference_plan.analysis: injury + experimenter (+ interaction check).
pitfalls: One technician tests all injured, the other all sham

notes: Planning recommendation only.

prompt: The drug worked in males (p < 0.05) but not in females (p = 0.2). Can we say the effect is male-specific?

source.citation: Garcia-Sifuentes & Maney 2021, eLife 10:e70817
source.basis: Sex-specific claims need an interaction test

reference_plan.design: Analyse as a 2 x 2 factorial; a future study should be powered for the interaction.
reference_plan.layout: n/a (analysis question).
reference_plan.replication: Interaction tests need much larger n than main effects.
reference_plan.randomization: n/a.
reference_plan.analysis: y ~ drug * sex; report the interaction estimate and CI.
pitfalls: Comparing p-values between sexes is not a test of difference

notes: Answer: not without testing drug x sex.

prompt: Maternal high-fat diet during pregnancy; then I test 3 pups per litter at 8 weeks. 6 dams per diet.

source.citation: Lazic, Clarke-Williams & Munafò 2018, PLoS Biol 16:e2005282
source.basis: Only 22% of parent-treated studies used the correct unit

reference_plan.design: Diet randomized to dams; n = 6 litters per diet.
reference_plan.layout: Record pup sex; balance sexes per litter where possible.
reference_plan.replication: Add dams, not pups; 2-3 pups per litter adds little power.
reference_plan.randomization: Diet to dam; testing order randomized.
reference_plan.analysis: y ~ diet (+ sex) + (1 | litter).
pitfalls: Reporting n = 18 pups per diet

notes: Planning recommendation only.

prompt: Lifespan of wild-type Dahomey females on 3 yeast concentrations.

source.citation: Piper & Partridge 2016, Methods Mol Biol 1478:291-302
source.basis: Standard density, 48 h mating, 100-150 flies per treatment at 10-15 per vial, rearing-bottle blocking

reference_plan.design: make_vial_allocation(): e.g. 15 rearing bottles, each supplying one vial of 10 females to each diet (150 flies per diet).
reference_plan.layout: Vials in random tray positions; trays rotated in the incubator by block; 25 C, 65% RH, 12:12 LD.
reference_plan.replication: Vials are the units for diet; flies are subsamples.
reference_plan.randomization: Bottle-to-vial allocation balanced; tray positions random.
reference_plan.analysis: Mixed Cox model: Surv ~ diet + (1|vial); log-rank as a check.
pitfalls: Uncontrolled larval density
Virgin vs mated females mixed
Different food cooks per diet

notes: Mate 48 h after emergence, then sort sexes.

prompt: Our mutant line lives 40% longer than Canton-S. Is that enough to publish?

source.citation: Toivonen et al. 2007, PLoS Genet 3:e95
source.basis: Indy effect vanished after backcrossing and Wolbachia clearance

reference_plan.design: Backcross the mutation >=6 generations into your control background, test Wolbachia in both lines, then rerun with vial design.
reference_plan.layout: As in the standard vial lifespan design.
reference_plan.replication: 100-150 flies per genotype per sex, repeated in an independent cohort.
reference_plan.randomization: Rearing-bottle blocks.
reference_plan.analysis: Mixed Cox model with vial random effect.
pitfalls: Comparing a mutant to an unrelated wild-type stock

notes: Not yet: background and cytoplasm first.

prompt: We overexpress a gene with da-GAL4 > UAS-geneX and compare lifespan to wild type.

source.citation: Burnett et al. 2011, Nature 477:482-485
source.basis: dSir2 effect vs wild type disappeared vs transgenic controls

reference_plan.design: Three genotypes: da-GAL4/+, UAS-geneX/+ and da-GAL4 > UAS-geneX, all in the same backcrossed background.
reference_plan.layout: Standard vial lifespan design.
reference_plan.replication: 100-150 flies per genotype per sex.
reference_plan.randomization: Rearing-bottle blocks.
reference_plan.analysis: Experimental line must differ from BOTH parental controls.
pitfalls: Wild type as the only control

notes: Insertion and background effects can mimic overexpression effects.

prompt: Measuring wing size in 2 mutants vs a control. I set up crosses with 8 females per vial overnight and measure the offspring.

source.citation: microPublication Biology 2023 (larval density and pupal size); Clancy & Kennington 2001
source.basis: Pupal size falls with ~25 extra larvae per vial

reference_plan.design: Several replicate vials per genotype at a fixed larval density (pick e.g. 30-50 first-instar larvae per vial).
reference_plan.layout: Vials of all genotypes in each tray; same food cook.
reference_plan.replication: Replicate vials per genotype; measure a fixed number of flies of each sex per vial.
reference_plan.randomization: Vial positions random within trays.
reference_plan.analysis: y ~ genotype * sex + (1|vial).
pitfalls: Egg-lay density varying by genotype fecundity
Pooling sexes

notes: Mutant fecundity differences change density and hence size.
